name.local: Techstars Tokyo

summary.en: Techstars' first Japan accelerator (launched 2024 in Tokyo). A sector-agnostic, ~3-month cohort program selecting 12 pre-seed/seed startups per class, investing $120,000 per company for ~5% common stock plus an uncapped MFN SAFE. Powered by Mitsui Fudosan and JETRO Startup, culminating in a Demo Day.

summary.en: Open Network Lab (Onlab), launched by Digital Garage in April 2010, is Japan's first seed accelerator. It has supported 164 alumni companies across Japan and Global tracks.

summary.en: Antler's Japan arm (Tokyo, launched 2023) runs a generalist, day-zero pre-seed program: a 6-week full-time residency in Tokyo followed by investment of $150,000 ($100K for 10% equity plus a $50K uncapped SAFE). strategy.thesis: Tokyo edition of the Silicon Valley enterprise-focused Alchemist Accelerator. Backs distinctive, technical founding teams building B2B/B2B2C enterprise tech with global potential, bridging Japan and the San Francisco Bay Area.

summary.en: Alchemist Japan is the Tokyo edition of the Silicon Valley Alchemist Accelerator, focused on enterprise/B2B tech founders with global ambitions. It runs a ~3-month in-person Tokyo program (25+ startups/cohort) with a follow-on phase in the SF Bay Area, investing net USD $70K for 8% equity (up to $100K) plus $500K+ in partner credits, ending in an invite-only Showcase. Supported by JETRO, Mitsubishi Estate and One Capital.

Power Angels is the operating community behind Yamamoto's Japan Angel Investor Association.

name.local: Japan Angel Fund

strategy.thesis: Syndicate-style fund where ~10 prominent founder-angels ('scouters') each independently source deals from their own allocation (no veto from others). Returns split LPs 50% / sourcing scouter 40% / remaining scouters 10%; scouters contribute no personal capital. Aim: maximize angels' know-how and influence across the startup ecosystem and build a PayPal-Mafia-style knowledge network in Japan.

application.how_to_apply: Founders are sourced directly by individual scouter-angels from their personal networks; no public open application.

summary.en: A 2018 syndicate-style fund of ~300M yen organized by ten prominent founder-angels (incl. Candle, Fablic, Spotlight, Coach United and Eureka founders). Each 'scouter' independently deploys part of the fund with no veto from peers; returns split 50/40/10 between LPs, the sourcing scouter and the rest. Built to circulate startup know-how and seed a PayPal-Mafia-style network in Japan.

name.en: Japan Investment Corporation for Carbon Neutrality (JICN)
name.local: 株式会社脱炭素化支援機構

aum.raw: 資本金 651.5億円 (capital ~JPY 65.15 billion, as of recent)

strategy.thesis: Public-private investment corporation established under the revised Global Warming Countermeasures Act to supply risk capital (equity, mezzanine) to a broad range of decarbonization businesses — renewable energy, storage, hydrogen, circular economy, sustainable agriculture — toward Japan's 2050 carbon-neutral goal.

summary.en: JICN (Japan Investment Corporation for Carbon Neutrality) is a government-private investment body established October 28, 2022 under the revised Global Warming Countermeasures Act, with initial capital of JPY 20.4 billion (half government industrial investment, half from 82 private firms) and current capital around JPY 65.15 billion. It supplies risk capital to decarbonization businesses and is a major LP in Japan's climate VC funds (ONE Innovators, EEI Booster, UMI).
summary.local: 2022年10月28日設立の官民ファンド。改正地球温暖化対策推進法に基づき、設立時資本金204億円（国の産業投資102億円・民間82社102億円）、現在の資本金は約651.5億円。脱炭素事業へリスクマネーを供給し、国内クライメートVCの主要LPでもある。

summary.en: A-FIVE (Agriculture, forestry and fisheries Fund corporation for Innovation, Value-chain and Expansion Japan), established November 2013 as a 20-year time-limited public-private fund, supported 6th-industrialization ventures combining primary agri/forestry/fishery operators with secondary/tertiary partners, mainly through regional sub-funds with local banks (51 sub-funds totaling ¥743.02B approved by end-2014, A-FIVE share ¥371.51B). summary.en: Japan's first cybersecurity-industry-specialized investment fund, established 1 April 2024. Security companies pool capital as LPs to invest in and grow other domestic security companies. General partner is WERU Investment; founding LPs are Kanematsu, Kanematsu Electronics (KEL) and Global Security Expert (GSX). summary.en: Spiral Capital is a Tokyo-based VC founded in 2016 (independent since 2017) investing in X-Tech (internet x real-world industry). Its 'BIG4' focus is Smart Infrastructure (incl. summary.en: Headline Asia (formerly Infinity Ventures / IVP), founded 2008 by Akio Tanaka and Hirofumi Ono and HQ'd in Tokyo with offices in Taipei and Beijing, is the Asia arm of the global Headline VC network. It invests early-to-growth across fintech, e-commerce, software/SaaS, developer tools, open-source, digital health and Web3 in Japan, SEA and India. summary.en: Miraido (ミライドア) operates the Robot Fund, a Kyoto-based vehicle focused on robotics and manufacturing-related startups. strategy.thesis: Sovereign wealth/public investment institution under METI that strengthens Japan's industrial competitiveness via open innovation, deploying risk capital through a fund-of-funds and direct fund subsidiaries (venture growth, buyout, multi-strategy).

summary.en: Japan Investment Corporation (JIC) is a Japanese sovereign-wealth-style investment institution established on 25 September 2018 under METI's Industrial Competitiveness Enhancement Act, succeeding the original Innovation Network Corporation of Japan. It was set up with ~¥2 trillion (~$18B) across four funds and had ~¥1.85 trillion total assets as of March 2024. JIC operates as a holding company over fund subsidiaries including JIC Venture Growth Investments and JIC Capital, and retains INCJ as a legacy-portfolio subsidiary.

investment.raw: STS phase up to ¥500 million; PCA phase up to ¥1 billion+ per project (grant)

program.eligibility: Deep tech startups requiring long-term R&D and large-scale funding to commercialize high-risk innovative technology contributing to carbon neutrality, resource circulation, economic security, etc.

summary.en: The NEDO Deep-Tech Startups Support Program (DTSU) is a Japanese government grant fund, established FY2023 with a planned ~¥93 billion budget running to FY2034, operated by NEDO (a national R&D agency). It provides non-dilutive, phased grant support to deep tech startups across STS (early R&D, up to ~¥500M), PCA (late R&D), and DMP (mass-production demonstration) phases. It is implemented alongside the Japanese SBIR push.
summary.local: NEDOのディープテック・スタートアップ支援事業（DTSU）は、2023年度に造成された政府の補助金基金（FY2023～FY2034、予算約930億円）。STS（実用化研究開発前期、上限約5億円）、PCA（後期）、DMP（量産化実証）の各フェーズで、長期かつ大規模な研究開発を要するディープテック・スタートアップに非希薄化型の助成を行う。日本版SBIRと連携して実施される。

summary.en: JETRO (Japan External Trade Organization) is a government-related independent administrative institution under METI, reorganized in its modern form in 1958. Since 2013 it has run startup-acceleration and global-expansion support: it backs 700+ Japanese startups per year via 15 acceleration programs and 3,000+ through mentoring, operates the Global Acceleration Hub in ~30 cities, and runs the J-Bridge platform connecting Japanese and overseas companies. It is a non-equity support provider, not an investor.

name.en: Japan Finance Corporation (JFC) — New Business / Startup Support Loan
name.local: 日本政策金融公庫 新規開業・スタートアップ支援資金

aka: 新規開業・スタートアップ支援資金

strategy.thesis: Wholly government-owned policy-finance institution providing low-interest startup/new-business loans (debt, non-dilutive) to founders, with no minimum self-funding requirement after 2024 reforms.

investment.raw: Loan limit ¥72 million (incl. ¥48 million working capital)

program.eligibility: Those newly starting a business or within approximately 7 years of business commencement; individuals and corporations; no self-funding requirement.

summary.en: Japan Finance Corporation (JFC), a government-owned policy-finance institution (formed 2008), offers the 'New Business / Startup Support Loan' (新規開業・スタートアップ支援資金) to founders. The loan ceiling is ¥72 million (including ¥48 million working capital), available to those within ~7 years of starting a business. A March 2024 reform abolished the old new-business loan scheme and removed the self-funding requirement, making it easier to access. This is debt financing, not equity.
summary.local: 日本政策金融公庫（JFC、2008年設立の政府全額出資の政策金融機関）は、創業者向けの「新規開業・スタートアップ支援資金」を提供。融資限度額は7,200万円（うち運転資金4,800万円）で、事業開始後おおむね7年以内が対象。2024年3月に旧「新創業融資制度」を統合し自己資金要件を撤廃した。出資ではなく融資（デット）。

summary.en: The Organization for Small & Medium Enterprises and Regional Innovation (SMRJ / 中小機構) is a national independent administrative institution (established 2004) supporting Japanese SMEs and startups. Its Startup Challenge Support service provides free expert consultations (Zoom/Teams, ~1 hour, nationwide) to startups and prospective founders aiming for IPO or M&A, covering business planning, capital policy, legal matters, stock options and impact business. SMRJ also operates incubation facilities. Non-dilutive support, not an investor.
summary.local: 独立行政法人中小企業基盤整備機構（中小機構／SMRJ、2004年設立）は、中小企業・スタートアップを支援する国の機関。スタートアップ挑戦支援事業では、IPOやM&Aを目指すスタートアップ・起業予定者向けに、事業計画・資本政策・法務・ストックオプション・インパクト事業等についてオンライン（Zoom/Teams、約1時間、全国対応）で無料の専門相談を提供。インキュベーション施設も運営する。出資は行わない。

program.eligibility: Foreign nationals intending to start a business in Japan, applying via a participating local government / METI-approved program.

summary.en: The Startup Visa (Program to Promote Startup Businesses by Foreign Nationals) is a METI-backed scheme letting foreign entrepreneurs receive a special 'Designated Activities' residence status to do preparatory activities for founding a business in Japan, issued via participating local governments. As of January 2025 it became available nationwide with the maximum preparation period extended to 2 years. It is a regulatory/immigration support program (no funding), serving as a stepping stone to the Business Manager visa.
summary.local: スタートアップビザ（外国人起業活動促進事業）は、経済産業省所管の制度で、外国人起業家が日本での起業準備のために「特定活動」の在留資格を取得できる仕組み。自治体経由で運用され、2025年1月から全国で利用可能となり、準備期間が最長2年に延長された。資金提供は行わない、入管・制度面の支援であり、経営・管理ビザへの足掛かりとなる。

summary.en: Tokyo Innovation Base (TIB), backed by the Tokyo Metropolitan Government, is a startup campus and ecosystem hub in central Tokyo opened in 2024, built around the '10×10×10 Innovation Vision' to increase Tokyo's unicorns, startups and public/private startups tenfold over five years. The TMG also runs SusHi Tech Tokyo (Sustainable High City Tokyo), Asia's largest innovation conference, whose 2024 Global Startup Program drew 40,206 participants. Non-equity ecosystem support, not an investor.
summary.local: Tokyo Innovation Base（TIB、東京イノベーションベース）は、東京都が運営する都心のスタートアップ拠点で、2024年に始動。「10×10×10イノベーションビジョン」のもと、5年でユニコーン・スタートアップ・官民連携を10倍に増やすことを目指す。都はアジア最大級のイノベーションイベントSusHi Tech Tokyo（Sustainable High City Tokyo）も主催し、2024年のGlobal Startup Programには40,206人が参加した。出資を伴わないエコシステム支援。

summary.en: The Cool Japan Fund (Overseas Demand Development Support Organization), established November 2013 under a dedicated METI-affiliated law, is a public-private fund capitalized at roughly ¥105.3 billion (public + private, e.g. Dentsu and others). It invests in businesses that expand overseas demand for Japanese content, food, fashion, media and lifestyle, including growth-stage companies. It has faced significant accumulated losses (reported ~¥30.9 billion deficit as of 2022). More content/expansion-focused than a pure startup investor.

summary.en: Globis Capital Partners (GCP), founded in 1996, is one of Japan's largest and oldest independent hands-on VCs, with cumulative AUM exceeding US$1.8 billion (~¥180B). Its largest fund, GLOBIS Fund VII, final-closed at ¥72.7 billion in 2022 with up to ¥10B investable per company, and it opened a San Francisco office to support portfolio globalization. Under its 'first to last' policy it leads rounds from early through growth/later stage. Notable winners include Mercari, GREE and SmartNews.

summary.en: WiL (World Innovation Lab) is a US-Japan growth-stage VC founded in 2013 by Gen Isayama (ex-DCM) and Masataka Matsumoto, with offices in Palo Alto and Tokyo. In June 2022 it raised over $1 billion in additional capital — including its third growth fund, WiL Ventures III, and Strategic Partners funds — taking total commitments across all funds above $1.9 billion. Its US investing concentrates on later-stage (Series B+) B2B SaaS. Portfolio includes 15 unicorns; public exits include Mercari, Asana, Wise, Raksul and Auth0 (acquired by Okta).

name.local: 日本アジア投資株式会社（JAIC）

aka: JAICクリプトアセットファンド

funds.name: JAICクリプトアセットファンド (JAIC Crypto Asset Fund)

strategy.thesis: Established Japanese VC (JAIC) that launched two dedicated 2025 vehicles: the JAIC-Web3 Fund targeting domestic listed Web3 (NFT etc.) companies, and the JAIC Crypto Asset Fund targeting crypto-asset-related companies — enabled by Japan's 2025 LPS-law reform allowing crypto holdings.

summary.en: Japan Asia Investment Co. (JAIC), a long-established Tokyo VC, formed two dedicated 2025 funds: the JAIC-Web3 Fund (¥465M as of Jul 2025) for domestic listed Web3/NFT companies, and the JAIC Crypto Asset Fund (¥2,480M as of Sep 2025) for crypto-asset companies — among the first to use Japan's reformed LPS rules.
summary.local: 老舗VCの日本アジア投資（JAIC）が2025年に組成した2つの専門ファンド。Web3（NFT等）国内上場企業向けの「JAIC-Web3ファンド」（2025年7月時点 465百万円）と、暗号資産関連企業向けの「JAICクリプトアセットファンド」（2025年9月時点 2,480百万円）。改正LPS法を活用した先行事例。
